primary_claim: Replicating Greenblatt's no-CoT filler-token/problem-repeat evals on Opus 4.5 reproduces the original trends and quantitative values, and newer models (Claude Fable 5, Opus 5, GPT-5.6-Sol) show substantially higher single-forward-pass (no chain-of-thought) latent reasoning performance, e.g. Fable 5 reaches 87.6% accuracy on Gen-Arithmetic with 10 problem repeats (vs ~60% previous SOTA) and GPT-5.6-Sol more than doubles its 3-hop baseline accuracy (6.2%->13.0%) with repeats.

effect.metric: accuracy on no-CoT single-forward-pass eval (Gen-Arithmetic/Comp-Math/2-Hop/3-Hop) under repeat/filler-token augmentation
effect.value: Fable 5: 87.6% Gen-Arithmetic w/10 repeats vs ~60% previous SOTA; GPT-5.6-Sol: 58.6%->83.4% Gen-Arithmetic (20 repeats), 6.2%->13.0% 3-Hop (repeats); Opus 4.5: 13.0%->31.1% 2-Hop (filler tokens)

stated_future_work: More comprehensive replications of previous work and open-source tooling for single-forward-pass eval elicitation in following posts
Include Gemini models once a consistent no-CoT elicitation technique is found for adaptive reasoning models
Narrow down a technique to consistently and robustly elicit no-CoT behavior from adaptive reasoning models
limitations_stated: No model performs better than chance on 4-hop questions or receives significant uplift from filler tokens/repeats, so 4-hop results are excluded from the main results

Adaptive-thinking-only models (Fable 5, Opus 5) cannot have reasoning explicitly disabled via API, so no-CoT elicitation relies on a forced structured-tool-call workaround that cannot fully rule out hidden reasoning not surfaced by the API
0.99% of Fable 5 and 0.13% of Opus 5 responses still showed signs of reasoning within the response text and were simply scored as incorrect rather than excluded
quote: Fable 5 gets 87.6% accuracy on Gen-Arithmetic with 10 problem repeats whereas previous SOTA around 60%.
